title: Soil Health Management, Soil Testing Protocol & Micronutrient Guidelines
source: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DAC&FW)
content: Soil testing is the only scientific basis for balanced fertilizer application. Soil samples must be taken in a zigzag pattern across the field, collecting 10-15 sub-samples at 0-15 cm depth for field crops and 0-30 cm for horticultural crops. Mix thoroughly and composite to 500 grams using quartering method. Key soil parameters: Soil pH (<6.5 acidic, 6.5-7.5 neutral, >8.5 alkaline/sodic), Electrical Conductivity (EC <1.0 dS/m normal), Organic Carbon (OC <0.5% low, 0.5-0.75% medium, >0.75% high). Major nutrients: Available N (low <280 kg/ha, med 280-560 kg/ha), P2O5 (low <10 kg/ha, med 10-25 kg/ha), K2O (low <110 kg/ha, med 110-280 kg/ha). Secondary & Micronutrients: Critical limits: Zinc 0.6 ppm (DTPA-extractable), Iron 4.5 ppm, Boron 0.5 ppm. Soil amendments: For acid soils (pH <5.5), apply agricultural lime or dolomite based on lime requirement test. For sodic soils (pH >8.5, ESP >15%), apply gypsum based on gypsum requirement test. Mandatory rule: Never apply uncalibrated chemical fertilizers without testing soil; over-application of urea leads to groundwater nitrate contamination and soil acidification.
